sections.heading: Regret: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive
sections.body:
To regret the past, use *ojalá* + **pluperfect subjunctive** (*hubiera* + participle): *Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.* (I wish I had studied more.) *Ojalá no te hubiera dicho nada.* (I wish I hadn't told you anything.)

Other ways: *Me arrepiento de…* (I regret…) + infinitive or noun: *Me arrepiento de no haber viajado más.* *¡Qué lástima que no hubieras venido!* (What a shame you hadn't come!) *Si lo hubiera sabido…* (If I had known…).

sections.heading: Reproach: deberías haber…
sections.body:
To reproach someone (or yourself) about the past, use the conditional of *deber* + *haber* + participle: *Deberías haber llamado.* (You should have called.) *No deberías haberle dicho eso.* (You shouldn't have told him that.) *Debí haberlo pensado antes.* (I should have thought of it before — preterite of *deber* is also common in LatAm.)

Other reproaches: *¿Por qué no me avisaste?* (Why didn't you let me know?) *¡Me lo hubieras dicho!* (You could have told me!) *¡Mira que te lo dije!* (I told you so!) *Tendrías que haber pedido permiso.* (You should have asked permission.)

examples: I wish I had studied more.
Ojalá no te hubiera dicho nada.
I wish I hadn't told you anything.
Me arrepiento de no haber viajado más.
I regret not having traveled more.
What a shame you hadn't come!
Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría ido.
If I had known, I wouldn't have gone.
You shouldn't have told him that.
I should have thought of it before.
Why didn't you let me know?
I didn't take advantage of the opportunity.
